claims.claim: A Cloudinary signature is the sorted parameter string with the API secret appended and no separator, hashed with SHA-1 (or SHA-256). file, cloud_name, resource_type and api_key are never part of the string to sign. Cloudinary's worked example with secret 'abcd' and timestamp 1315060510 yields a21ad0f63beb4de2e5575204b79ab90bffb02c10, which the bundled script reproduces exactly.
claims.raw_snippet: Note file , cloud_name , resource_type , and api_key are never part of the string to sign, but are always part of the upload call.

claims.claim: The SDK methods use SHA-1 by default and SHA-256 is selected with the signature_algorithm configuration parameter set to sha256.
claims.raw_snippet: The SDK methods use the SHA-1 algorithm by default, but you can use the SHA-256 algorithm instead by setting the signature_algorithm SDK configuration parameter to sha256 .
